title: feat: feat: MCP progressive disclosure contract for all data-returning interfaces
description:
The development harness has multiple MCP interfaces that return structured data (sam_plan read, sam_plan ready, backlog_view entries, artifact reads). There is no platform-level contract defining how these interfaces must handle per-request token limits for AI agent consumption. Each tool either has no pagination at all (sam_plan read/ready) or a partial solution that still overflows on large data (backlog_view section filter overflowed at 112K chars even when filtering by section name during #2515 session work). AI agents working within token-limited contexts cannot reliably map (what does this data contain?), navigate (give me a bounded portion), or extract (give me this specific item) from MCP data-returning interfaces without risking context overflow.

**Scope underestimation — findings from #2515 feasibility gate (2026-05-31)**:

Initial scoping assumed the change was a read-path concern (add params to MCP tools). Feasibility work on #2515 revealed the impact is deeper:

1. `ready_tasks` pattern: 36 files contain this term across the development-harness plugin. The `TaskBackend.get_ready_tasks()` method in `sam_schema/core/task_backend.py` is the backend protocol that all 6 implementations (`local_yaml.py`, `memory.py`, `github_task.py`, `beads.py`, `gist_task_layer.py`, and the Gist layer) must satisfy. If pagination is part of the progressive disclosure contract, it likely changes the backend protocol signature — cascading to every implementation and the CLI.

2. `backlog_view` partial fix: PR #2495 added section-level filtering but a single large entry in a section still overflows budget (observed: RT-ICA section in #2515 at ~17K chars). The contract must address entry-level bounded reads, not just section selection.

3. Design question unresolved: the right progressive disclosure contract for AI agents navigating MCP data is not known. User proposals (TOC mode, page-number navigation, sub-section selection) are highly-rated candidates but have not been researched against how agents actually traverse plan and backlog data during implementation work. Whether pagination belongs at the MCP layer only (transparent to backends) or changes backend protocols is a key architectural decision.

**Blocks**: #2515 (sam_plan read/ready first implementation) cannot proceed to planning until this contract is defined.

**User-provided context**: contract should define a standard three-layer progressive disclosure pattern — map (TOC view of structure and contents), navigate (page-based access with current page and pages remaining), extract (item-by-ID access). This pattern should apply consistently to all existing and future MCP tools that return structured data.

**Reference designs (assessed 2026-05-31)**:

1. **mdsel-mcp** (https://github.com/dabstractor/mdsel-mcp) — strong architectural reference. One unified MCP tool with three behaviors from parameter presence: index mode (files only → TOC with available selectors), select mode (files + selector → bounded content extraction), search mode (fuzzy text → scored selector matches). Selector syntax is path-based and ordinal: `h2.1/code.0`, `namespace::h2.0`, with `?head=N`/`?tail=N` for size-bounded extraction. Clone and study — this is the clearest existing implementation of map/navigate/extract as a single stateless MCP tool. The CLI source shows how to generate agent-consumable TOCs and handle bounded extraction within per-request token limits.

2. **markdown-parser-py** (https://pypi.org/project/markdown-parser-py/) — reference for dot-path selector API design (`tree.find_node_by_path('Intro.Install')`). Weak as an implementation candidate (1 star, experimental, edge cases unsupported). For any markdown parsing in this codebase, use `marko` instead — it is already a declared dependency with established AST-walking patterns in `agentskills-linter`.

3. **marko** — already in this repo (`CLAUDE.md` explicitly references it), established patterns for walking AST, correct tool for any markdown parsing implementation needs.

**Prerequisite findings this item waits on**:

1. Clone and study `dabstractor/mdsel-mcp` and the underlying `mdsel` CLI — extract the specific design decisions that make its index/select/search pattern work for LLM consumption within MCP token limits.
2. Architecture decision: does pagination/selection live at the MCP response layer only (backends return full data, server slices/selects), or does it change the `TaskBackend` and `BacklogBackend` protocol methods? Each choice has different blast radius implications (36 files for TaskBackend vs ~5 for MCP layer only).
3. Inventory: full map of all data-returning MCP tools in the harness and their backend dependencies — to scope the adoption effort.
4. `backlog_view` entry-level gap: characterise what is needed to bound large single entries, and whether a selector/path approach (like mdsel's `h2.1/code.0`) is better than pure offset/limit for structured markdown data.

## Story

As a **developer using Claude Code skills**, I want to **feat: mcp progressive disclosure contract for all data-returning interfaces** so that **the tooling becomes more capable and complete**.

## Description

The development harness has multiple MCP interfaces that return structured data (sam_plan read, sam_plan ready, backlog_view entries, artifact reads). There is no platform-level contract defining how these interfaces must handle per-request token limits for AI agent consumption. Each tool either has no pagination at all (sam_plan read/ready) or a partial solution that still overflows on large data (backlog_view section filter overflowed at 112K chars even when filtering by section name during #2515 session work). AI agents working within token-limited contexts cannot reliably map (what does this data contain?), navigate (give me a bounded portion), or extract (give me this specific item) from MCP data-returning interfaces without risking context overflow. Tool-by-tool fixes applied ad-hoc produce inconsistent interfaces and repeat the same design work for every new tool.

**User-provided context**: the contract should define a standard three-layer progressive disclosure pattern — map (TOC view of structure and contents), navigate (page-based access with current page and pages remaining), extract (item-by-ID access). This pattern should apply consistently to all existing and future MCP tools that return structured data. #2515 is planned as the first implementation of this contract on sam_plan read/ready.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Work matches description
- [ ] Plan or implementation complete

## Context

- **Source**: Session observation — #2515 implementation, 2026-05-31
- **Priority**: P1
- **Added**: 2026-05-31
- **Research questions**: None

## Groomed (2026-06-01)

### Concerns

Pre-existing concerns in progressive_markdown/ surfaced during 2026-05-31 code review — must be addressed as part of implementing the progressive disclosure contract:

1. **ProgressiveDisclosure vs MarkdownNavigator unified output** — two systems with divergent output contracts (dict with next_call hint vs Pydantic NavigationResult with no hint). Architecture decision: both should return NavigationResult; ProgressiveDisclosure's raw dict return is the mistake. Unification belongs in the plan for this item, not ad-hoc.

2. **AmbiguousSectionRefError never raised** — resolve_section() silently returns first match on slug collision; docstrings and public API surface advertise the exception as raised. Either raise it or remove it from the API surface.

3. **MarkdownIndexer.build() monolith** — 150 lines, 74 statements, 40 locals (PLR0915/PLR0914). Needs decomposition into _process_heading_token(), _process_fence_token(), _finalise_sections(), _BuildState dataclass.

4. **__init__.py docstring stale** — still shows qualified import path after chunk_text/paginate_results were added to package-level __all__.

<!-- artifact-gist:14a1aaea8ff101f14c5e0abf35e0d4a5 -->

## RT-ICA

RT-ICA Final: MCP progressive disclosure contract for all data-returning interfaces
Date: 2026-05-31
Goal: Define and implement a platform-level progressive disclosure contract (map/navigate/extract) with backlog_view reference implementation, unblocking #2515.

**Decision: APPROVED**

| # | Condition | Status | Evidence |
|---|-----------|--------|---------|
| 1 | Reference design studied (mdsel-mcp) | AVAILABLE | `.tmp/scratch/reports/mdsel-mcp-study.md` — parameter-presence routing, ordinal dot-path selectors, head/tail bounded extraction, graceful truncation documented |
| 2 | Pagination layer: MCP only vs backend protocol | AVAILABLE | tool-inventory confirmed 0 backend protocol changes required; all 8 tools can be handled at MCP response layer only |
| 3 | Full inventory of in-scope MCP tools | AVAILABLE | `.tmp/scratch/reports/mcp-tool-inventory.md` — 43 tools, 8 need pagination, 1 canonical backend method (not 36 files) |
| 4 | Entry-level bounding mechanism | AVAILABLE | User decision: path-based ordinal dot-notation (mdsel/markdown-parser-py native). Flat map, no indentation. Ordinal IS the navigate selector. |
| 5 | progressive_markdown/ concerns diagnosed | AVAILABLE | `.tmp/scratch/reports/progressive-markdown-analysis.md` — 4 concerns with exact file paths, line numbers, fix plans. Implementation work (not a planning prerequisite). |
| 6 | Contract document | DERIVABLE | Will be produced during implementation (it IS the deliverable). Discovery artifact defines the full spec. |
| 7 | Testable acceptance criteria | AVAILABLE | 11 testable ACs in discovery artifact, grounded in real fixture content from #2515 (51 sections, 112K chars), #2521, #996, #1857. |
| 8 | #2515 sequencing | AVAILABLE | User decision: contract + backlog_view reference implementation both required before #2515 proceeds. |

**DERIVABLE assumptions to carry forward:**
- Ordinal path construction for nested headings (flat `sections_index` vs nested body) is a design question for the architect — does not block planning
- `head=N` tokenisation unit (tiktoken vs char-with-factor) is an architect decision — does not block planning
- Silent-fallback fix backward-compat: caller migration path is an architect concern — does not block planning
